concepts.title: Electric Current and Potential Difference
concepts.definition: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge through a conductor, measured in amperes by an ammeter connected in series; charges flow because a potential difference set up by a battery pushes them, and a voltmeter connected in parallel measures this difference in volts.
concepts.key_idea: Charge per second is current; the potential difference is its push.
concepts.textbook_ref: jesc111.txt sections 11.1-11.2 (electric current and circuit, potential difference)

concepts.title: Ohm's Law - Current, Voltage and Resistance
concepts.definition: Ohm's law states that at constant temperature the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it: V = I times R, where R is the resistance; resistors that obey it are ohmic, and resistance depends on the material, length, area and temperature.
concepts.key_idea: V equals I times R: double the push and the flow doubles, if temperature stays put.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh111 ohm's law sections of jesc111

solution_steps.explain: Ohm's law gives the potential difference.

concepts.title: Series and Parallel Circuits
concepts.definition: Resistors in series add directly and carry the same current, sharing the voltage; resistors in parallel share the same voltage and their reciprocals add, so the equivalent resistance drops below the smallest - two ways to wire a circuit with opposite effects.
concepts.key_idea: Series adds resistance, parallel adds conductance: wiring decides the total.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh111 sections on resistors in series and parallel

concepts.title: Heating Effect and Electric Power
concepts.definition: Electric power is the rate of doing electrical work, P equals V times I, measured in watts; the energy dissipated as heat in time t is I squared R t - the heating effect behind toasters and fuses, billed commercially as kilowatt-hours.
concepts.key_idea: V times I is power; I squared R t is the heat that warms the toaster.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh111 sections on heating effect and electric power
question_patterns: find the power of the appliance operating at the given voltage and current

solution_steps.explain: Power equals V times I in watts.
